articles.title: Clinical and radiological outcomes of pediatric distal tibial physeal fractures: a retrospective analyses from a single institution.
articles.authors: Kar I, Tasci M, Ozer M, Ardali D, Soylemez MS
articles.population: Children with distal tibial physeal fractures
articles.outcomes: Premature physeal closure, fracture healing time, American Orthopedic Foot and Ankle Society scores
articles.take_home: Premature closure of the growth plate occurred in 26% of children with distal tibial fractures, particularly in younger children and those with slower healing, but did not significantly affect clinical outcomes during mid-term follow-up. Most children (96%) had good or excellent functional results.

articles.title: Ulnar Epiphysiodesis for Distal Radius Physeal Arrest: Comparing Early Detection to Late Presentation Management.
articles.authors: O'Brien A, Campbell TR, Bomar JD, Edmonds EW
articles.population: Children under 18 years with premature physeal arrest of the distal radius treated with ulnar epiphysiodesis
articles.outcomes: QuickDASH scores, SANE (Single Assessment Numerical Evaluation) scores, and final ulnar variance measured at mean 6.4 years follow-up
articles.take_home: Children who had ulnar epiphysiodesis for premature distal radius arrest had similar functional outcomes regardless of whether surgery was done early before deformity developed or later after deformity was present. The study suggests that correcting any deformity is more important than the timing of treatment.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Boxer's Fracture and Aggression, Hyperactivity, and 2D:4D Finger Ratio in Children and Adolescents: A Prospective Case-Control Study.
articles.authors: Ozel V, Gunaydin F, Daglar S, Dursun G, Yilmaz M
articles.population: Children and adolescents aged 6 to 17 years
articles.outcomes: 2D:4D finger ratio, aggression scores (physical aggression, anger, hostility), ADHD symptoms
articles.take_home: Children with boxer's fracture had lower finger ratios, higher aggression levels, and more ADHD symptoms than those with other injuries. The study suggests boxer's fracture may indicate underlying behavioural or neurodevelopmental concerns that warrant screening.

articles.title: The Role of Perfusion MRI in Detecting Avascular Necrosis of the Femoral Head in Children: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Manoj NJ, Yip J, Bridgens A, Rastogi A, Siebachmeyer M, Huttman M, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of diagnostic and prognostic studies
articles.population: Children under 18 years with hip disorders including developmental dysplasia of the hip, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, and Legg-Calve-Perthes disease
articles.sample_size: 538 patients across 567 hips in 13 included studies
articles.outcomes: Sensitivity 90%, specificity 60%, positive predictive value 58%, negative predictive value 90% for perfusion MRI in detecting avascular necrosis; associations between femoral head hypoperfusion and worse radiographic outcomes
articles.take_home: Perfusion MRI shows promise for early detection of avascular necrosis in children with certain hip problems and may predict which children will develop worse hip damage, but more high-quality research is needed before it can be used routinely in clinical practice.

articles.title: Retrospective cohort study assessing radiological outcomes and risk factors for progression of femoral head osteonecrosis in children with sickle cell disease, following bisphosphonate therapy, CD-BMAC and proximal femoral reorientation osteotomy.
articles.authors: Elayedatt RA, Gahukamble AD, A AM, Thuppale VE, Abraham A, Kandagaddala M, et al.
articles.population: Children with sickle cell disease and femoral head osteonecrosis
articles.outcomes: Radiological progression of femoral head osteonecrosis measured by Steinberg stage at final follow-up (mean 30.7 months)
articles.take_home: Three treatments - bisphosphonates, core decompression with bone marrow concentrate, and proximal femur reorientation osteotomy - all prevented disease progression in children with early-stage femoral head osteonecrosis. In advanced cases with femoral head collapse, proximal femur reorientation osteotomy performed better than the other two treatments.

articles.title: Epidural analgesia in labour and neonatal and childhood outcomes: national population based cohort study.
articles.authors: Kearns RJ, Kyzayeva A, Singh S, Lawlor DA, Shaw M, Nelson S
articles.population: Women in labour with singleton pregnancies delivering vaginally or via unplanned caesarean birth in NHS hospitals in Scotland
articles.outcomes: Neonatal neurological morbidity, other neonatal morbidity, neonatal sepsis, Apgar score less than 4 at five minutes, neonatal mortality at 28 days, and childhood cerebral palsy
articles.take_home: The study found no link between epidural pain relief in labour and harm to newborns or children, including brain problems, infection, low oxygen levels, death, or cerebral palsy. Epidural analgesia appears to be a safe pain relief option during labour.

articles.title: Trampoline Fractures in Children.
articles.authors: Parviainen R, Laaksonen T, Grahn P, Sinikumpu JJ, Helenius I, Ahonen M
articles.study_type: Case series analysis of registry data
articles.population: Children and adolescents aged 0 to 15 years with trampoline-related fractures in the Helsinki area, Finland
articles.sample_size: 1153 trampoline-related fractures (592 girls, 561 boys) from a registry of 18,279 total fractures
articles.outcomes: Location of fractures, fracture severity, need for surgery, comparison of open fractures with other sports-related fractures across three age groups (0 to 5, 6 to 10, and 11 to 15 years)
articles.take_home: Trampoline fractures in children vary by age, with younger children typically sustaining simpler lower leg fractures and older children more commonly experiencing severe forearm fractures. Trampoline injuries overall carry a higher risk of displaced or open fractures compared to other sports injuries.

articles.title: Assessing Correlations Between PROMIS-25 and QuickDASH in Pediatric Patients With Upper Extremity Trauma.
articles.authors: Kelly N, Sang L, Coufal S, Swarup I
articles.population: Paediatric patients with upper extremity trauma
articles.outcomes: Correlation between PROMIS-25 domains and QuickDASH scores; floor and ceiling effects; variation by sex, age, race/ethnicity, and operative timing
articles.take_home: PROMIS-25 and QuickDASH questionnaires measure similar aspects of upper limb function in injured children, with strong correlations for physical function and pain. PROMIS-25 may be better for tracking recovery after surgery, whilst QuickDASH may be more useful for children who are recovering well.

articles.title: Early-Stage Perfusion MRI Correlates Significantly With Femoral Head Deformity in Children Under 6 Years of Age With Legg-Calve-Perthes Disease: A Preliminary Multicenter Study.
articles.authors: Lee J, Mistry A, Cao J, Agonias K, Morris W, Shah H, et al.
articles.population: Children under 6 years old with early-stage Legg-Calve-Perthes disease
articles.outcomes: Correlation between early perfusion MRI hypoperfusion and femoral head deformity measures (deformity index, epiphyseal index, sphericity deviation score) at 2-year follow-up and healed stage
articles.take_home: In young children with Legg-Calve-Perthes disease, reduced blood flow to the femoral head on early MRI scans correlates with worse hip shape outcomes later on. A hypoperfusion level of 60% or higher on MRI may help identify children at higher risk of developing a misshapen hip joint.

articles.title: Correlation Between Radiographic Parameters and Clinical Range of Motion in Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis.
articles.authors: Streeter SR, Ullmann OC, Sarkar S, Sankar WN
articles.population: Children with stable slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) treated with in situ pinning
articles.sample_size: 74 hips in 69 patients (mean age 12.3 years, 50.7% male)
articles.outcomes: Relationship between radiographic parameters (Southwick slip angle, posterior sloping angle, percent epiphyseal displacement, alpha angle) and clinical range of motion (flexion, abduction, internal rotation)
articles.take_home: The amount of slip displacement has the strongest effect on hip motion, with each 1% increase in displacement reducing flexion and abduction by about 2 degrees. Surgeons should prioritise correcting the degree and angle of the slip to preserve hip movement in children with this condition.

articles.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty in Patients With Open Triradiate Cartilage: 10-Year Follow-Up of an Expanded Cohort.
articles.authors: Selemon NA, Reuter ZC, Varas-Rodriguez E, Sierra RJ, Trousdale RT, Grigoriou E
articles.population: Patients with open triradiate cartilage undergoing total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 24 patients (24 hip replacements), mean age 14 years
articles.outcomes: 92% of implants showed stable integration; all patients achieved independent walking with average Harris Hip score of 92; two patients needed acetabular component revision for aseptic loosening
articles.take_home: Hip replacement in young patients with open triradiate cartilage (growing hip bone) produced excellent results with 92% of implants remaining stable over 10 years and patients walking independently without aids. The study suggests it is safe to perform hip replacement in these young patients without waiting for the cartilage to mature.

articles.title: Screw start point and orthogonal relationship to the physis do not impact clinical outcomes for in-situ fixation of slipped capital femoral epiphysis.
articles.authors: Eltayeby HH, Stelzer JW, Tamburini L, Lee MC
articles.population: Children with slipped capital femoral epiphysis treated with in-situ screw fixation
articles.sample_size: 177 patients (83 with anterior screw starting point, 94 with lateral screw starting point)
articles.outcomes: Hip pain, early complications, reoperations, and radiographic parameters including screw position and physis crossing
articles.take_home: Whilst anterior screw starting points resulted in more orthogonal screw positioning compared with lateral starting points, neither the screw starting point nor how perpendicular the screw was to the growth plate affected pain levels, complication rates or the need for further surgery.

articles.title: Single Versus Double Pin Fixation of the Calcaneocuboid Joint During Calcaneal Lengthening Osteotomy for Pediatric Idiopathic Flatfoot.
articles.authors: Bae K, Kwak YH, Kang MS, Ryu S, McCranie A, Ahn JH, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 9 to 15 years with idiopathic flexible flatfoot undergoing calcaneal lengthening surgery
articles.outcomes: Radiographic angles and calcaneocuboid joint subluxation index measured at 3 months, 1 year and 2 years after surgery
articles.take_home: Using two pins instead of one to stabilise the calcaneocuboid joint during flatfoot surgery helped maintain better foot alignment at 2 years, although both methods were similarly effective at preventing joint slipping.

articles.title: A Quality Initiative for Posterior Spinal Fusion in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS): Liposomal Bupivacaine With Dexamethasone Use Results in Substantial Reduction in Inpatient Opioid Use.
articles.authors: Stuedemann A, Huston M, Saddler N, Anderson J, Benvenuti M, Sherman AK, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective quality initiative comparing postoperative analgesia protocols
articles.population: Adolescents aged 10 to 18 years with idiopathic scoliosis undergoing posterior spinal fusion
articles.sample_size: 159 patients (88 intrathecal morphine, 36 intravenous methadone, 35 liposomal bupivacaine with dexamethasone)
articles.outcomes: Inpatient opioid use (morphine milligram equivalents per kilogram), length of hospital stay, and pain scores
articles.take_home: Young people who received liposomal bupivacaine and dexamethasone without patient-controlled analgesia needed much less strong painkiller after spinal fusion surgery and left hospital sooner, with pain control just as good as other methods. This suggests this approach is a better way to manage pain after this operation whilst reducing reliance on opioid medications.

articles.title: Outcomes of Distal Radius Autograft in Adolescent Scaphoid Nonunion Repair.
articles.authors: Rupp GE, Rea PM, Curran PF, Bomar JD, Edmonds EW, Wallace CD
articles.population: Adolescents with scaphoid fracture nonunion
articles.outcomes: Union achieved in all wrists at mean 3.3 months post-surgery; improved carpal alignment; 94% returned to activities at mean 9.6 months
articles.take_home: Surgery to repair scaphoid nonunion using a bone graft from the wrist worked well in adolescents, with all patients achieving bone healing and most returning to sport within about 10 months. The wrist alignment improved significantly after surgery.

articles.title: Serial Casting and Hinged Elbow Bracing in the Treatment of Fixed Flexion Deformity of the Elbow Following Obstetric Brachial Plexus Palsy.
articles.authors: Simpson AI, Kwok IH, Liechti R, Sinisi M, Panagiotidou A, Fox M
articles.population: Children with obstetric brachial plexus palsy and fixed flexion deformity of the elbow
articles.outcomes: Mean improvement in elbow flexion deformity of 25.2 degrees (from 45.8 degrees to 20.7 degrees); 65.2% achieved post-treatment deformity of 20 degrees or less; 9% premature termination; 15.1% required repeat treatment
articles.take_home: Serial casting and hinged elbow bracing significantly improved elbow straightening in children with birth-related nerve injuries, with most children needing only one course of treatment. The techniques were safe and effective even when repeated in the small number of children whose deformity returned.

articles.title: Brace non-adherence and relapse after Ponseti treatment for idiopathic clubfoot: a focused updated scoping review.
articles.authors: Arvati S, Zokou H, Luc F
articles.population: Children with idiopathic clubfoot treated with Ponseti method
articles.sample_size: 25 studies (19 empirical and 6 contextual/grey-literature items from focused update)
articles.outcomes: Brace adherence, relapse after correction, factors associated with non-adherence including missed visits, brace interruption, transportation burden, caregiver understanding, and continuity of care
articles.take_home: Children who do not wear their brace as instructed after clubfoot correction are more likely to have their feet relapse. Important factors affecting whether families stick with bracing include transport difficulties, understanding of care instructions, whether visits are kept, and how well organised the treatment team is.

articles.title: Fracture morphology and multidirectional instability in failed closed reduction of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures.
articles.authors: Darilmaz MF, Bulut M
articles.population: Children aged 2-12 years with severe upper arm bone fractures (Gartland type III or IV supracondylar humerus fractures)
articles.outcomes: Success of closed reduction versus need for open surgery; association between fracture type, instability patterns, age, and time to surgery with closed reduction failure
articles.take_home: Flexion-type fractures and certain patterns of instability seen during surgery were strongly linked to failed closed reduction attempts. Surgeons may be able to better predict which children will need open surgery by recognising these fracture patterns beforehand.

articles.title: Rock-paper-scissors-OK game for neurological examination in pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: A prospective randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Aydin T, Inci F, Kilic M, Yigit N, Kahve Y, Ceyhan E
articles.population: Children aged 4-10 years undergoing surgery for supracondylar humerus fractures
articles.outcomes: Preoperative and postoperative nerve examination time, child and parent satisfaction (Child HCAHPS questionnaire), behavioural compliance (agitation, crying, noncompliance)
articles.take_home: Children taught nerve examination using a smartphone game-based method (rock-paper-scissors-OK) adapted better and had faster postoperative assessments than those taught by traditional methods. Children using the app-based method were calmer during examination and families reported better communication with doctors.

articles.title: Five-year MRI follow-up of growth-related complications after ACL reconstruction in children and adolescents.
articles.authors: de Pesters C, Laval A, Staali L, Flumian C, Faruch M, Accadbled F
articles.study_type: Prospective single-centre case series with MRI follow-up
articles.population: Children and adolescents with open growth plates undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Tibial and femoral physeal angles, Harris growth arrest line deviation, physeal bone bridge formation, skeletal maturity, premature physeal closure. Angular deviations of 5 degrees or more found in 37.5% of cases but were minimal (range -6 to +5 degrees). Bone bridges observed in three patients (18.8%) and resolved spontaneously. No premature physeal closure identified.
articles.take_home: Growing children who have ACL reconstruction surgery using a standard technique through the growth plates showed minimal changes on MRI scans over five years, with no clinically important growth problems. The study suggests this type of surgery is safe in children with open growth plates.
